q: 1. Two projects having the same status expect payback period which project will be selected?
options: The project having more payback period
The project having less payback period
All off all of the above
explain: If everything else is equal, the project that recovers its investment sooner (shorter payback period) is preferred because it carries less risk and returns cash faster.

q: 2. The number of year from commissioning of the project at which net operating benefit equals to the investment is called ......
explain: Payback period is the time, counted from commissioning, after which cumulative net operating benefit equals the investment.

q: 3. The number of years required for the net operating benefit to pay back the initial cost of project is called ......
explain: This is the definition of payback period: years needed for net operating benefits to recover the initial cost.

q: 4. For the selection of a project B/C ratio should be ......
explain: A project is acceptable when present worth of benefits exceeds present worth of costs, i.e. B/C > 1.

q: 5. In a project selection, minimum B/C ratio should be ......
explain: The minimum (threshold) B/C ratio is 1, where benefits just equal costs. Note: strictly, B/C above 1 is preferred; the key gives the threshold value.

q: 6. If NPV is +ve then, NFV is ......
explain: NFV = NPV x (1+i)^n, and (1+i)^n is always positive, so NFV has the same sign as NPV.

q: 7. Two projects having same status except pay back period. Which project will be selected?
options: the project having more pay back period
the project having less pay back period
explain: A shorter payback period is preferred as it recovers the initial investment faster.

q: 8. Pay back period is counted only after
options: starting of the construction of the project
completion of the construction of the project
explain: Recovery of costs begins once the project is operational and generates revenue (commissioning).

q: 9. Benefit cost ratio is the ratio of
explain: The B/C ratio compares the Present Value of Benefits to the Present Value of Costs.

q: 10. For the selection of a project B/C ratio should be
explain: A project is viable if benefits exceed costs, i.e., the ratio is greater than 1.

q: 11. At what condition project is good ......
options: IRR equal to the discount rate
explain: If IRR is greater than the discount rate, NPV at that discount rate is positive, so the project is good.

q: 12. The benefit cost ratio is
options: no any relation with discount rate
explain: As the discount rate increases, the present value of future benefits decreases more significantly than initial costs, lowering the B/C ratio.

q: 13. For the selection of any project which criteria is followed ......
explain: IRR, NPV and B/C ratio are all standard criteria for project selection.

q: 14. For selection of the project net present value should be ......
explain: A project is selected when its NPV is positive, meaning benefits exceed costs.

q: 15. In a project selection ERR should be ......
explain: The key marks ERR > 0 (a positive external rate of return) as the condition for selection.

q: 16. For accepting of project, the minimum value of benefit cost ratio should be
explain: For a project to be minimally acceptable, BCR must be at least equal to one (benefits at least cover costs).

q: 17. Find the NPV if initial investment 5,000, Benefit for three years = 3000 per year and discount rate = 9%.
18. For any project to be feasible ......
options: annual worth should be equal to zero
payback period should be equal to or less than 5 year
explain: A project is feasible when its present worth is positive.

q: 19. At what condition, project is good
explain: The discount rate represents the required return; if the IRR is higher, the project adds value to the firm.

q: 20. For the selection of the project, NPV should be
explain: A positive NPV indicates that the project earns more than the discount rate and adds value.

q: 21. In case of project selection which one is considered?
explain: Multiple indicators are typically used to gain a comprehensive view of project viability.

q: 22. In FW method, the minimum condition which the project is feasible is
explain: Similar to PW, the Future Worth (FW) must be positive (or zero) for a project to be economically justified.

q: 23. The internal rate of return (IRR) is a rate of return used in capital budgeting to measure and compare the .....of investments.
explain: IRR is used in capital budgeting specifically to measure and compare the profitability of different investment options.

q: 24. In any project 10 million rupees is invested to get an income of 1 million. Then the invested money of 10 million is called
explain: Investment represents money leaving the entity (expenditure), which is a cash outflow.

q: 25. During calculation of IRR, NPV should be
explain: The Internal Rate of Return is defined mathematically as the discount rate that makes the NPV exactly zero.

q: 26. Another name for Net Present Value (NPV) is
explain: Net Present Value (NPV) is also commonly referred to as Net Present Worth (NPW).

q: 27. In any study the details of project are given below: Project a1=10.8%, a2=15.8%, a3=11%. Which project will be selected?
explain: The project with the highest Internal Rate of Return (15.8%) is the most economically attractive choice.

q: 28. Net Present Value (NPV) is defined as the total present value (PV) of .......of cash flows:
explain: NPV is defined as the total present value of the net amount of cash flows (inflows minus outflows) over the project's life.

q: 29. A project is said to be feasible when its net present value (NPV) is
explain: Per the answer key, a project is considered feasible when its NPV is greater than one (i.e., positive/greater than the threshold value).

q: 30. In project selection ERR should be
explain: The Economic Rate of Return (ERR) must be positive and typically higher than the social discount rate for a project to be selected.

q: 31. If benefit cost ratio of a proposed project is 0.95 then project is ......
options: financially not feasible but may or may not economically viable
explain: B/C below 1 means the project is not financially feasible, but wider economic benefits may still justify it.

q: 32. If net present value of a project is zero at a discount rate of 12% then IRR of project is ......
explain: IRR is the rate at which NPV equals zero, so IRR is 12%.

q: 33. If two projects are mutually exclusive than
options: The one with the higher NPV should be chosen
The one with the positive NPV should be chosen
The one with the negative NPV should be chosen
explain: For mutually exclusive projects (only one can be chosen), the project with the higher NPV should be selected as it creates more value.

q: 34. A project is said to be feasible when its Net present value (NPV) is
explain: A project is considered feasible when its NPV is greater than one (positive), as marked in the answer key.

q: 35. Net present value (NPV) is a term widely used in :
explain: NPV is a fundamental tool for analyzing the total discounted costs and benefits of a project over time.

q: 36. If the investments a firm makes would ............ value from the firm, it means that NPV < 0.
explain: A project with NPV < 0 is expected to cost more than it returns, thus 'subtracting' value from the firm.

q: 37. In some of the road Project connecting the district headquarters are implemented even its IRR is not satisfactory, because of ......
explain: Such roads are built to meet social need even when the IRR is low.

q: 38. The decession rule for project acceptance is that :
explain: The standard rule is to accept a project if its yield (IRR) is at least equal to the Minimum Acceptable Rate of Return (MARR).

q: 39. Which among the following is not true about benefit cost analysis?
options: cost and benefits must be converted to a common time base
a public project is normally acceptable if the B-C ratio is at least one
the analysis makes sure that the benefits are at least 10-20% more than the costs
the B-C ratio is a ratio of discounted benefits to discounted costs
explain: There is no universal rule requiring a 10-20% buffer; the basic requirement is simply a ratio of 1.0 or higher.
